title: Who is Doctor Doom, and why is Iron Man playing him?
description: Doctor Doom's comic origin and why Marvel cast Robert Downey Jr. as the villain of Avengers: Doomsday.

lines.text: July 2024. Hall H, San Diego Comic-Con.
More than six thousand fans watch a line of masked men in green cloaks walk onto the stage.
Then one of them takes off his mask.
It's Robert Downey Junior. Iron Man himself.
And he tells the crowd: new mask, same task.
The man who spent eleven years as Marvel's greatest hero,
who died on screen saving the universe,
is coming back as the villain who wants to rule it.
His name is Victor von Doom.
And to understand why Marvel made this bet, you need two stories.
The story of the most dangerous man in Marvel Comics.
And the story of the year Marvel's master plan fell apart.
One is sixty years old. The other is still happening.
And they're about to collide on December 18th.
Rewind to 2019.
Avengers: Endgame closes out eleven years of Marvel movies,
and makes nearly two point eight billion dollars.
For a while, it's the biggest movie ever made.
Now Marvel needs a new villain. Someone bigger than Thanos.
They choose Kang the Conqueror: a man who rules across time itself.
A version of him appears in Loki in 2021.
Kang himself arrives in Quantumania in 2023.
And at Comic-Con 2022, Marvel announces the movie it's all leading to:
Avengers: The Kang Dynasty, set for May 2025.
Marvel had built its next saga around one villain: Kang.
Then it starts to crack.
Quantumania opens big, then fades fast, with brutal reviews.
In March 2023, the actor playing Kang, Jonathan Majors, is arrested in New York.
Then, in December 2023, the actor who played him is convicted of assault and harassment.
Marvel drops him the same day.
And the whole plan comes down.
Years of story, and no villain at the centre.
Marvel needed someone new.
But the answer was already sixty years old.
July 1962. Stan Lee and Jack Kirby introduce a new villain in Fantastic Four number five.
Meet... Doctor Doom.
In his very first story, Doom kidnaps the Invisible Woman,
and forces the rest of the team into his time machine,
to steal Blackbeard's treasure for him.
The Thing ends up becoming Blackbeard.
That's Doom from day one. He doesn't just fight heroes. He makes them work for him.
Within ten years, he's fought the Avengers, Spider-Man, Iron Man and Daredevil.
His origin comes two years later.
Victor von Doom is born in Latveria, a tiny kingdom in the mountains of Europe, to a Romani family.
His mother, Cynthia, is a witch. She dies when he's a baby.
His father, Werner, is a healer.
When he can't save the Baron's dying wife, he runs with his son into the snow,
and freezes to death.
Alone, Victor finds his mother's secret: a chest of magic.
And he swears revenge.
He grows up brilliant. So brilliant, a university in America offers him a scholarship.
At Empire State University, Victor builds a machine to reach the realm of the dead, and speak to his mother.
His classmate, Reed Richards, spots a flaw in the calculations.
Victor ignores him.
The machine explodes in his face.
He's expelled. And he blames Reed, forever.
In the first comics, the scar is tiny: Jack Kirby drew a small mark on his cheek.
But to Victor, his face is ruined.
He travels to Tibet, where monks teach him their secrets,
and there, he forges his armor.
In one famous retelling, he puts on the mask while it's still red-hot.
Victor goes home, and takes the throne of Latveria.
From that day, he has one name. Doctor Doom.
So why is Doom such a big deal? Start with this: he's a king.
A head of state, with diplomatic immunity. The heroes can't just arrest him.
He's one of the smartest men on Earth. And a sorcerer.
He builds robot copies of himself, Doombots,
so you never know if you're fighting the real one.
And every year, he fights the Devil himself, for his mother's soul.
He once stole the power of the Silver Surfer.
In 1984's Secret Wars, he steals the power of the Beyonder, a being so powerful he's practically a god.
For a moment, Doom holds the universe in his hand.
In 2015, he goes even further. When the multiverse ends, Doom saves what's left,
stitches it into one patchwork world called Battleworld,
and rules it as God Emperor Doom.
And at the very end, Reed Richards does what Victor never could. He heals his face.
And in 2025, after taking the title of Sorcerer Supreme from Doctor Strange, he does it again.
Overnight, Doom takes over the whole world, and names himself its emperor.
That's the story Marvel's next two Avengers movies are building toward.
And here's the twist. In 2016, while Tony Stark lay in a coma,
Doom put on the armor, and became Iron Man.
Doom has already been Iron Man once.
So why Robert Downey Junior?
Four months before Hall H, he'd just won his first Oscar, for Oppenheimer.
And Doom has been on the big screen before.
Julian McMahon played him twice for Fox, in 2005 and 2007.
Toby Kebbell played him in 2015.
Fans have waited a long time for a Doom that feels like the comics.
Because Doom is Tony Stark's dark mirror.
Both are geniuses. Both hide inside metal suits. Both have enormous egos.
Tony learned to use his for other people. Victor never did.
Marvel brought back the directors who made Endgame, Joe and Anthony Russo.
And according to Variety, Downey's deal is worth more than eighty million dollars.
But how can the X-Men and the Fantastic Four even be in an Avengers movie?
In 2019, Disney bought Twenty-First Century Fox, and with it, the film rights to both.
In 2025, The Fantastic Four: First Steps brought Marvel's first family home.
And Doom comes with them.
The trailers show the X-Men from the old Fox movies, the Fantastic Four, and Steve Rogers, back.
And in the trailer, Sue Storm says it simply: he used to be different.
Avengers: Doomsday arrives on December 18th. Secret Wars follows in December 2027.
Whatever Victor von Doom wants this time, one thing is certain.
He has never settled for saving the world.
Back in Hall H, the man who played Iron Man lifts the mask one more time.
New mask. Same task.
